title: Polar Bears
keyIdea: Polar bears live only in the Arctic, the frozen far north. Penguins live in the south, so the two never meet in the wild. A thick layer of fat called blubber keeps a polar bear warm, even when it swims in icy water. Its thick fur looks white, but its skin is black. Big wide paws spread its weight on thin ice and work like paddles. Polar bears catch seals by waiting very still by a hole in the sea ice where a seal comes up to breathe. When the sea ice melts in summer, they wait on land and eat very little.
familyTip: Try a blubber glove at home. Fill a bowl with water and ice. Put some solid fat, such as lard or vegetable shortening, between two sandwich bags. Put one hand in a bag with fat and one bare hand into the water, and see which feels cold first. Then talk about why a polar bear needs its blubber.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: send the bear north, test a blubber glove, try paw sizes on thin ice, wait at a breathing hole, find the months with no sea ice.

kid: Polar bears live in the Arctic. That is the far north of the world, near the North Pole. Much of it is sea that freezes into ice. Penguins live in the south, so polar bears and penguins never meet in the wild.

The Arctic is very cold. A polar bear has thick fur, and its skin under the fur is black. Under its skin is a thick layer of fat called blubber. When the bear swims, wet fur keeps out much less cold. The blubber keeps it warm in the icy water.
A polar bear has very big paws. On thin ice, big paws spread the bear's weight, so the ice does not crack. In the sea, the front paws work like paddles. Polar bears are strong swimmers.

Polar bears eat seals. Seals swim faster than bears, so a bear does not chase them in the water. A seal must come up to a hole in the ice to breathe. The bear waits by the hole, very still and quiet, for a long time. When the ice melts in summer, the bear cannot reach the seals. It waits on land and lives off its fat until the sea freezes again.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This fits the National Curriculum in England for Years 1 and 2: identify and name a variety of common animals, and identify how animals are suited to their habitats. It also fits NGSS K-LS1-1 (what animals need to survive) and 2-LS4-1 (living things in different habitats). Key words: Arctic, North Pole, habitat, sea ice, blubber, insulation, fur, paw, prey, predator, seal, breathing hole.

Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) live only around the Arctic Ocean, in Canada, Alaska, Greenland, Norway and Russia. Their blubber can be over 10 cm thick, and it is their main protection from cold in water, because wet fur loses much of its insulation. Their fur hairs are not white pigment; they scatter light and look white over black skin. Paws can be about 30 cm across. Ringed and bearded seals are their main prey, and the commonest way to catch them is still-hunting: waiting at a breathing hole or at the ice edge. The blubber glove times in the lab are for illustration only, in line with the classroom experiment.

Common mistakes: thinking polar bears live in the Antarctic with penguins; thinking fur alone keeps them warm in the water; thinking the skin is white; thinking bears catch seals by chasing them in open water, when seals are faster swimmers; and thinking big paws make a bear lighter, rather than spreading the same weight over more ice. The lab, the practice and the challenge target each of these.

On Hudson Bay in Canada the sea ice melts in summer, and the bears wait on land for about four months, from around mid-July to mid-November, eating very little. That ice-free time is now several weeks longer than it was in the 1980s, which is why scientists watch sea ice so closely. In the lab your child sends a polar bear, a penguin and an Arctic fox home, tests four gloves in icy water, tries five paw sizes on thin ice and in the sea, waits by the right breathing hole, and finds the months with no sea ice.

choices: In the Arctic, the far north
practice.hint: Think of the North Pole. Which end of the world is it?
practice.explain: Polar bears live only in the Arctic, the far north. Penguins live in the south.

practice.prompt: A polar bear swims for {n} hours in icy water. What keeps it warm?
choices: A thick layer of fat called blubber
practice.hint: Think of the blubber glove. What kept the hand warm in the icy water?
practice.explain: Wet fur keeps out much less cold, so in the water the thick layer of blubber keeps the bear warm.

practice.prompt: How does a polar bear catch most seals?
choices: It waits by a breathing hole in the ice
It chases them under the water
It digs them out of the snow
practice.hint: Seals swim faster than bears. Where must a seal come up?
practice.explain: A seal has to come up to a hole in the ice to breathe, so the bear waits there, still and quiet.

practice.prompt: A polar bear has 4 paws. A mother bear and her {n} cubs walk on the ice. How many paws is that?
practice.hint: Count the bears first: the mother and {n} cubs. Each bear has 4 paws.
practice.explain: That is {=n+1} bears, and {=n+1} lots of 4 paws is {=4*(n+1)} paws.

practice.prompt: Why do big paws help a polar bear on thin ice?
choices: They spread its weight over more ice
practice.hint: The bear weighs the same. What changes with bigger paws?
practice.explain: The same weight is spread over a bigger patch of ice, so the thin ice is less likely to crack.

pool.prompt: Do polar bears and penguins meet in the wild?
choices: No, bears live in the north and penguins in the south
Yes, they share the same ice
pool.hint: Where do polar bears live? Where do penguins live?
pool.explain: Polar bears live in the far north and wild penguins live in the south, so they never meet.

choices: A thick layer of fat under the skin
pool.hint: It is under the skin and keeps the bear warm.
pool.explain: Blubber is a thick layer of fat under the skin. It keeps the bear warm, even in icy water.

pool.prompt: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
pool.hint: The fur looks white. The skin under it is a different colour.
pool.explain: A polar bear's skin is black. Its thick fur looks white over the top.

pool.prompt: A polar bear waits {n} hours by a breathing hole. Then it waits 2 more hours. How many hours is that?
pool.hint: Start at {n} and count on 2 more hours.
pool.explain: {n} hours and 2 more is {=n+2} hours. Polar bears are very patient hunters.

pool.prompt: Why does a polar bear not chase seals in the sea?
pool.hint: Polar bears can swim. Who is faster in the water?
pool.explain: Polar bears are good swimmers, but seals are faster, so the bear waits for a seal to come up to breathe.

pool.prompt: What does a polar bear do when the sea ice melts in summer?
choices: It waits on land and eats very little
It hunts seals in the open sea
pool.hint: It hunts seals from the ice. What happens with no ice?
pool.explain: With no sea ice it cannot reach seals, so it waits on land and lives off its fat.

pool.prompt: There are {n} polar bears on the ice. What do their front paws do when they swim?
pool.hint: Big front paws push the water back.
pool.explain: All {n} bears use their big front paws like paddles to push through the water.

pool.prompt: Why does the sea ice matter so much to polar bears?
pool.explain: The breathing holes are in the sea ice, so the ice is where polar bears catch seals.

pool.prompt: Which is the best way to keep warm in icy water?
pool.hint: Think of the blubber glove test.
pool.explain: A thick layer of fat keeps out the cold best in water. Wet fur and bare skin lose heat fast.
